content.title: About
content.content: Sandwich spread is a ready‑to‑eat paste made from plant‑based and/or dairy ingredients, designed for spreading on bread, rolls, and other baked goods. It has a smooth texture, mild flavor, and is often enriched with herbs, spices, and aromatics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial sandwich spread appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a cheaper alternative to butter.
More than 30 flavor variants exist: classic, garlic, herb, olive, cheese, and even sweet versions with berries.
Most modern spreads are vegan and contain no animal fats.
Sandwich spread is frequently used in making sandwiches, wraps, and canapé appetizers.

items.title: Rich in plant oils
items.content: Spreads based on olive or sunflower oil provide monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Formulations often include B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, which aid normal energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Herbs and spices such as rosemary and basil add antioxidant properties.

items.title: Convenient energy source
items.content: Its high calorie density makes it a quick source of energy, useful for active individuals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Some versions are fortified with probiotics or fermented ingredients that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The product may contain nuts, soy, or dairy, which are common allergens.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Certain spreads contain up to 1 g of salt per 100 g, which may be unsuitable for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of its high energy density, portion control is advised, especially on weight‑management diets.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some commercial spreads use artificial preservatives that can cause sensitivity in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread it on bread, toast, baguette, or use as a filling for wraps and sandwiches. It can also be mixed into sauces, salad dressings, or used as a base for hot open‑face sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the spread refrigerated at 2 °C–6 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. After opening, use within 2–3 weeks. Discard if the smell, taste, or appearance changes or if mold appears.
